Sundhedsklynge Bornholm is a local healthcare cluster operating within [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] in Denmark [^src4] [^src6]. It serves as a key geographic and organizational unit for monitoring and evaluating the quality of care for patients with [[atrieflimren]] across the national healthcare system [^src1]. 

In the annual quality reports published by the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP), the cluster's performance is measured against several national clinical indicators. For Indikator 1, which assesses the timely initiation of [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] for newly diagnosed AF patients, Sundhedsklynge Bornholm achieved a result of 91.0%, successfully meeting the standard [^src1]. However, the cluster fell short on [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]], which tracks the use of echocardiography, scoring 78.1% and failing to meet the target threshold [^src2]. 

Long-term treatment persistence is also closely monitored. For the period between July 2018 and June 2019, the proportion of AF patients receiving continuous anticoagulation treatment was recorded at 80.0% [^src4]. The cluster's data is further integrated into broader national analyses, including the geographic distribution of ischemic stroke incidence ([[indikator-5|Indikator 5]]) [^src5], severe bleeding events [^src7], and heart failure outcomes [^src8]. 

Geographically, Bornholm's results are mapped alongside other Danish clusters—such as [[sundhedsklynge-byen|Sundhedsklynge Byen]], [[midtklyngen|Midtklyngen]], and [[sundhedsklynge-fyn|Sundhedsklynge Fyn]]—to visualize regional variations and identify areas needing quality improvement [^src5] [^src10]. While some clusters in Northern and Central Jutland consistently meet development targets, others, including those with lower performance levels hovering around 85%, highlight the ongoing challenges in standardizing AF care nationwide [^src10].
